clue.text: Fighting over centre court sale

indicators.note: the fighting word is laid over and around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: fighting means action, as in soldiers seeing action

indicators.note: centre asks for the middle letter of the five-letter word court

explanation.surface: Combat breaks out on the main court while something is being sold off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' puts the fighting word round U, the middle of 'court'.
explanation.definitionFit: An auction is a public sale where goods go to the highest bidder.

clue.text: Helped by answer being soundly concealed

indicators.note: soundly signals that the next word is taken by how it is pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: concealed means veiled, covered as if by a veil

explanation.surface: Someone was assisted by a reply that was well hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soundly' turns VEILED into the sound-alike spelling VAILED.
explanation.definitionFit: To have availed someone is to have been of use or benefit to them.

clue.text: Revolution covering working with meteorological phenomenon

indicators.note: covering means the revolution word wraps around the working word

parts.note: a revolution is one complete cycle, a turn round
working means switched on, operating

explanation.surface: A spinning motion combines with weather to make a striking natural event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' is the container signal: the revolution word wraps around the working word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyclone is a rotating storm system, a weather event studied by meteorologists.

clue.text: Silly old relative taken in by hollow invective

indicators.note: taken in by means the relative sits inside the other letters
hollow means the word invective is emptied, keeping only its first and last letters

parts.note: nan is a grandmother, an older relative

explanation.surface: A foolish elderly family member is drawn in by empty abuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hollow' empties a word to its first and last letters; 'taken in by' is the container signal. NAN is British slang for grandmother.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane describes something pointless and foolish, lacking sense.

clue.text: Steal identities from address forms?

parts.note: nick is British slang for steal
names are what identify people

explanation.surface: Identity theft pulled off by lifting details from forms carrying people's addresses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'address forms' reads like paperwork but means ways of addressing someone, the question mark flagging the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicknames are informal names people are called by, a familiar way of addressing them.

clue.text: Ghoulish horse seen around Hackney

indicators.note: seen around means the horse word encloses the Hackney word

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
a hackney carriage is the formal name for a cab, a taxi for hire

explanation.surface: A spooky horse is spotted roaming the east London district of Hackney.
explanation.walkthrough: Hackney is an area of London, but here it is the hackney carriage, the legal term for a London taxi.
explanation.definitionFit: Macabre means grim and gruesome, dwelling on death in a ghastly way.

clue.text: Conclusions to motorway repairs

indicators.note: to means the conclusions are attached on after the motorway letter

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1
conclusions means ends

explanation.surface: Roadworks on the motorway come to a close at last.
explanation.definitionFit: To mend something is to fix it, so the verb forms match.

clue.text: Dye firm using Chilean process

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: process means the letters of Chilean are worked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A dye company relies on a production method from Chile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'process' is the anagram signal, though it reads as a verb the firm uses.
explanation.definitionFit: Cochineal is a crimson colouring made from crushed insects, used to stain food and fabric.

clue.text: It offers protection from conflict in mass!

indicators.note: in places the conflict word inside the mass word

parts.note: bulk means mass, a large quantity
war is armed conflict

explanation.surface: Something shields people from fighting that breaks out among a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulwark is a defensive wall or safeguard.

clue.text: Energy lost because of work in door?

indicators.note: in places the work word inside the door word

parts.note: an entry is a door or way in
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Power seeps away because someone is busy working in the doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' as a musical opus is a standard abbreviation; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics, entropy measures the heat a system can no longer convert into useful work.

clue.text: Very old bridge — a singular start to crossing

parts.note: an arch is a bridge, or forms one
I is the first-person singular pronoun, and the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: start to asks for the first letter of the word crossing

explanation.surface: An ancient bridge offers a unique way to get across the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic means belonging to a much earlier period, antiquated.

clue.text: Connection with head allowed jewellery!

parts.note: the neck joins the head to the body
let means allowed, permitted

explanation.surface: Being linked with the boss gets someone permission to wear the gems.
explanation.definitionFit: A necklet is a short necklace, an ornament worn round the throat.

clue.text: They're often tied up with unfinished business

definitions.text: They're often tied up with unfinished business

parts.words: They're often tied up with unfinished business
parts.note: the phrase about tying things up when wrapping matters reads as dealing with leftover tasks, but loose threads are literally tied

explanation.definitionFit: Loose ends are details still outstanding, which people speak of tying up to finish a job.

clue.text: State of one possessed coming back with nothing?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: coming back means the possessed word is read from right to left

parts.note: possessed means had, owned
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone haunted returns empty-handed, wondering about their condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' is the reversal signal; 'possessed' reads as haunted but means owned.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the fifty US states.

clue.text: Father about to be overcome with fear

indicators.note: to be overcome means the about word is swallowed up inside the father word

parts.note: dad is an informal word for father
re means about, concerning, as in letter headings

explanation.surface: A father is on the point of being paralysed by terror.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' looks like 'on the point of', but 'about' is a separate piece and 'to be overcome' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is great fear or apprehension of something to come.

clue.text: Outfit unhappy with discipline

parts.note: a dress is an outfit
down means low in spirits, unhappy

explanation.surface: Someone is miserable with a strict regime about what they wear.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress someone down is to scold or reprimand them severely.

clue.text: How does one get into a flat?

definitions.text: How does one get into a flat?

parts.words: How does one get into a flat?
parts.note: the question seems to ask about renting an apartment, but asks what opens every door in a block

explanation.definitionFit: A master key opens many locks, such as all the apartments in a building.

clue.text: Begin with fish? Amazing!

parts.note: start means begin
ling is a long cod-like sea fish

explanation.surface: Opening a meal with fish proves astonishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Startling means surprising or astonishing.

clue.text: A spy spied trouble with illness

indicators.note: trouble means the letters of the spy phrase are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: An agent who was watched gets into difficulty and falls ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' is the anagram signal for the nine letters of 'A spy spied'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyspepsia is indigestion, a disorder of the stomach.

clue.text: Doctor has a way with one cold that's extreme

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A doctor has a remarkable way with someone who has a chill.
explanation.definitionFit: Drastic means severe or far-reaching, going to great lengths.

clue.text: Fish bite and people expect results, initially

parts.note: snap means bite, as a dog snaps

indicators.note: initially asks for the first letter of each of the three words that follow

explanation.surface: Fish bite, and anglers hope for a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes P, E and R from 'people expect results'.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapper is any of several sharp-toothed sea fish.

clue.text: Cuts around ring curls

indicators.note: around means the cuts word surrounds the ring letter

parts.note: lops means cuts off
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A hairdresser trims round the ringlets.
explanation.definitionFit: Loops are curves that turn back on themselves, like curls or coils.

clue.text: Scramble a goal — it could give you earache!

indicators.note: scramble means the letters of the next words are jumbled together

explanation.surface: A frantic goalmouth scramble might leave someone with sore ears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scramble' is the anagram signal for A GOAL and IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Otalgia is the medical term for pain in the ear.

clue.text: Female with a blood-stained cut

parts.note: she refers to a female
red is the colour of something stained with blood

explanation.surface: A woman has a gory wound.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheared means cut or clipped, as wool is sheared from sheep.

clue.text: Gather there's a church service

parts.note: Mass is the Catholic church service

explanation.surface: Worshippers come together for a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to collect or accumulate, to bring together.

clue.text: Customer support for a top range coming out

indicators.note: coming out means the letters of a top range emerge in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Shoppers are drawn by the launch of a premium product line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming out' is the anagram signal for A TOP RANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Patronage is the regular custom given to a shop or business by its customers.

clue.text: Guide one into bed!

indicators.note: into means the one letter goes inside the bed word

parts.note: a plot is a garden bed
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone helps a person climb into bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' is the flower bed, PLOT, not furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: To pilot is to steer or lead someone along a course.

clue.text: In London it's more than warm enough for this animal!

indicators.note: in London points to the Cockney habit of dropping the H at the start of words

parts.note: hotter means more than warm

explanation.surface: London summers are too hot for some creature.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, traditionally drop initial H, so HOTTER is said as 'otter'.
explanation.definitionFit: An otter is a fish-eating mammal of rivers and coasts.

clue.text: Earth summits need fuel!

parts.note: tops means summits, peaks
oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: Mountain peaks are in need of fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Topsoil is the upper layer of soil, the earth in which plants grow.

clue.text: Number entering illegally, not showing name

indicators.note: illegally means the letters are bent out of their lawful order
not showing means the name letter is left out of the word entering

explanation.surface: Someone sneaking into a country illegally keeps their name hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not showing' drops one N from ENTERING, leaving ETERING; 'illegally' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An integer is a whole number, with no fraction.

clue.text: Crown court imprisoning alternative individual

indicators.note: imprisoning means the court letters lock the other words inside them

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: The crown court jails an unconventional person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imprisoning' is the container signal; 'Crown court' reads as the English criminal court but splits into definition and abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A coronet is a small crown worn by nobles.

clue.text: Tabloid backing nation with flowers

indicators.note: backing means the tabloid word is read in reverse

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging name for a tabloid newspaper
a land is a nation, a country

explanation.surface: A popular newspaper supports the country with a floral display.
explanation.definitionFit: A garland is a wreath of blossoms worn or hung as decoration.
